title: Parameter-Efficient Periocular Fusion for Cross-Condition and Cross-Dataset Occlusion-Robust Face Verification
author: Pararajasingham Sangiya
target: IEEE Transactions on Biometrics, Behavior, and Identity Science
abstract: Face verification under masks and sunglasses requires representations that retain identity information across different visible regions. We compare frozen DINOv2 with a trained projection, whole-face LoRA, periocular LoRA, fixed dual-branch fusion, and learned fusion. Fifteen new models are trained on CPU for five complete epochs, using three seeds and a frozen 6,171-row ROF manifest that excludes exact-content duplicates and a confirmed cross-split near-identical photograph. On the new test pairs, periocular LoRA leads masked ROC-AUC (0.9221 +/- 0.0046), fixed fusion leads sunglasses AUC (0.8950 +/- 0.0021), and learned gating leads neutral AUC (0.9458 +/- 0.0026). Known training-name-overlap exclusion leaves 802 MFR2 pairs, on which gating achieves 0.9548 +/- 0.0022; exact-conflict exclusion leaves 21,798 exploratory RMFRD pairs, where fixed fusion achieves 0.7240 +/- 0.0099. Validation-calibrated operating points are distinguished from retrospective ROC summaries. Same-branch controls show that learned gating does not consistently improve on constant or permuted weights. A separate pretrained SFace baseline is stronger on several protocols, with different training and alignment. These findings support condition-dependent benefits of adaptation and complementary regions, while limiting claims about adaptive reliability, low-FAR deployment, and state-of-the-art performance.
keywords: Face verification, occlusion robustness, masked-face verification, periocular representation, DINOv2, LoRA, learned fusion, cross-dataset evaluation.
